insights.claim: Training Hub uses a Strategy pattern (Algorithm/Backend/Registry) that enables runtime-swappable training backends with fundamentally different execution models (torchrun, in-process, co-located vLLM).
insights.reasoning: The Algorithm base class, Backend base class, and AlgorithmRegistry factory form a classic Strategy pattern. Each backend (InstructLabTrainingSFTBackend, UnslothLoRABackend, ARTLoRAGRPOBackend, GEPABackend, MLflowGEPABackend) encapsulates a different execution model, from torchrun-distributed to single-GPU time-sharing. This pattern allows the library to grow its algorithm inventory without changing existing code paths.

insights.claim: The litellm dependency excludes versions 1.82.7-1.82.8 due to the TeamPCP supply chain attack (2026-03-24), indicating active supply chain risk awareness.
insights.reasoning: The explicit version exclusion `!=1.82.7,!=1.82.8` with the inline comment about the compromised versions shows the team actively monitors and responds to supply chain attacks in their dependency tree. This is a positive security signal but also highlights the risk surface of depending on litellm for LLM inference.

insights.claim: Training Hub has no service boundary or container image, inheriting all security, networking, and FIPS characteristics from the host environment.
insights.reasoning: As a pure Python library with no Dockerfiles or Kubernetes manifests, Training Hub's FIPS compliance, network policies, and authentication are entirely delegated to the consuming workload. This simplifies the library itself but means platform architects must ensure every host environment that imports training-hub meets FIPS and security requirements independently.
